interpretation: Even ablating only 9 late layers (20-28, roughly a third of the original 25-layer edit) reproduces the full IFE DEF collapse to exactly 0.0 -- the same qualitative signature as the full 25-layer edit. This suggests late layers specifically are responsible for the DEF-collapse effect identified as the real, statistically-robust signal (OGDA_random_control_statistical_summary.json), not simply 'how much of the network is touched.' RGU (own scenario) shows a smaller, different-direction FA movement than the 25-layer version (-0.017 vs +0.017), consistent with FA being an unreliable/noisy signal across different layer-range choices, while a much smaller late-layers-only edit is enough to reproduce the more robust DEF-collapse finding. Worth testing whether an even smaller late-layer window (e.g. just layers 24-28) still reproduces this, to localize the effect further -- not yet done.
